set_aside.subject: R0-89 loss boundary
set_aside.text: The restored store begins its own history from the backup: every change after it is lost
set_aside.question: After what event are changes lost: creation of the restored backup, successful checking of that backup, or loss of the store?
options: Every change committed after the backup snapshot is lost
Every change committed after the backup was successfully checked is lost
Only changes attempted after the store itself was lost are lost
set_aside.default_guess: Every change committed after the backup snapshot is lost

set_aside.subject: identities lost after backup
set_aside.text: every change after it is lost
set_aside.question: What happens when the lost changes include newly minted project, customer, room or pointer identities that consumer services or issued documents already reference?
options: Reintroduce the records under the same identities
Create replacement identities and require every consumer to relink them
Leave the identities permanently not found
Accept an explicit import or recovery operation for these identities
set_aside.default_guess: Create replacement identities and require every consumer to relink them, analogous to R0-79

set_aside.subject: replay guarantees across restore
set_aside.text: Registry's guarantees — the log's numbering, the closed import — hold within each store's history
set_aside.question: Does a request id previously accepted only in the lost history count as a retry after restoration, given R0-36 and R0-88 promise that retries do not create again and return what they made?
options: Treat it as new in the restored history
Refuse it because its previous outcome cannot be recovered
Preserve replay outcomes outside the restored store
Recover and return the result from the lost history by another mechanism
set_aside.default_guess: Treat it as new in the restored history

set_aside.subject: owner recovery record
set_aside.text: follows the owner's own record of the retention review
set_aside.question: What record is authoritative for recovery, what post-backup actions must it contain, and does it cover only erasures, restrictions and relationship endings or also their reversals and other lost state changes?
options: The external governance retention-review record, containing every retention-related action and reversal
A separate disaster-recovery journal maintained by the owner
Only the three actions explicitly named, with all other lost changes left unrecovered
set_aside.default_guess: Use the external governance retention-review record and require it to contain every retention-related action and reversal needed after the backup
